rationale: Everyone switches on the same day, so the natural design is a prospective observational study of the first six months, measuring adoption as completion without override (c2), completeness against a fixed checklist, reporting time and referrer views, with historic free-text reports rated by a pre-specified stated-or-implied rule (c3) as context. The multicentre study (c1) gives planning values.
alternatives: Before-after comparison with historic reports as the main analysis (refused as primary: the historic reports were not written for the checklist; kept as context)
Stepped introduction by radiologist (refused: the department has already fixed a single switch date)
guidelines: SQUIRE 2.0 for the description of the change
whyNotMoreComplex: A stepped or randomised introduction would need the switch date moved and would not change the department's decision.

decision.statement: Run a six-month prospective observational study of template use (completion without override), completeness of key elements for three index questions, active reporting time and referrer views after the 2027-01-11 switch, with historic free-text reports rated by a pre-specified stated-or-implied rule as context.
decision.question: How should the department evaluate the switch to structured abdominal CT reports?

criteria.text: Completeness gains and adoption patterns elsewhere give usable planning values and definitions.
A fair historic reference can be rated.

gates.requirement: Research office determination of the evaluation's status
gates.evidence: Service evaluation determination SE-2026-061 dated 2026-09-02, supplied by the investigator
Investigator constraint: one radiology registrar has 3 hours a week from January to July 2027

alternatives: Before-after comparison with historic reports as the main analysis
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3; both gates are met on supplied facts.

summary: Prospective observational study recommended; both gates met.
